en: The Ninth Bell
Find the pear seller in the square
Climb the bell tower and ring the old bell
zh_TW: 登上鐘樓，敲響那口舊鐘

en: Pull the trapped out of North Street
zh_TW: 把北街被困的人救出來

en: Find the swordswoman in white on Main Street
zh_TW: 去主街找那個白衣劍士

en: Get the wounded cart through the crossing
Go down to the pear seller's cellar
Noen
Pear Seller
Ada
Noen? Out on an eclipse night. Here — the last of this winter's pears.
zh_TW: 諾恩？月蝕夜還出門。來，今年最後一批冬梨。

en: Dad, your scale is leaning your way again.
zh_TW: 爸，你的秤又往自己那邊歪了。

en: Nonsense. This scale is more honest than the mayor.
zh_TW: 胡說，這秤比鎮長還老實。

en: Two, please.
My father always said your scale was off.
zh_TW: 我爸也老說你的秤不準。

en: I should go.
Two for the price of one and a half. Don't tell your dad.
zh_TW: 兩個算你一個半的錢。別跟你爸說。

en: He said it every time. And every time, he bought some anyway.
zh_TW: 他每回都這樣說，每回都還是買。

en: Because ours are the sweetest in Frostbridge. The scale has nothing to do with it.
zh_TW: 因為我們家的梨是霜橋鎮最甜的。跟秤沒關係。

en: Stay away from the bell tower tonight. The wind feels wrong.
zh_TW: 今晚別往鐘樓那邊去。風不對。

en: Late winter, the third eclipse. My guide said: nine strikes, and the door opens.
zh_TW: 冬末，第三次月蝕。我寫的攻略說：敲九下，門就會開。

en: One strike per breath. Don't miscount.
(Somewhere below, a dog starts barking.)
Before the ninth toll faded, North Street sank into the dark.
zh_TW: 第九聲還沒散，北街就整條沉進黑暗裡。

en: The guide never mentioned this part.
Strike the bell
Your father used to buy pears from us. He always said my dad's scale was off.
zh_TW: 你爸以前常來買梨，老說我爸的秤不準。

en: He always paid for one extra.
zh_TW: 他每次都多付一顆的錢。

en: ...Was it really off?
...I know. Dad always slipped one back into the bag.
zh_TW: ……我知道。我爸每次都偷偷多塞一顆回去。

en: (Ada presses a pear into your hand and says nothing.)
zh_TW: （艾妲把一顆梨塞進你手裡，什麼也沒說。）

en: You don't even remember that.
The way down to the under-city is in our cellar. I'll take you. Not because I forgive you.
zh_TW: 通往地底城的入口在我家地窖。我帶你去。不是因為我原諒你。

en: Sheila
Journal
{key} Close
The price of restoring
(cut away)
Beneath the South Street Arch
Father waited for me under that arch every day after school. He'd hide behind a pillar and make me find him.
zh_TW: 那座拱門，是父親每天接我放學時等我的地方。他會躲在柱子後，故意讓我找。

en: That evening he bought a hot sweet potato and broke it in two, the bigger half for me. "If you can't find me, wait under the arch. I'll always come out." "What if you never do?" "Then it's your turn to hide, and I'll come looking."
zh_TW: 那個傍晚，他買了一個熱薯，掰成兩半，大的給我。「找不到我的時候，就在拱下等。我一定會出來。」「要是你一直不出來呢？」「那就換你躲，換我來找。」

en: His face is still there. The taste of the sweet potato is still there.
zh_TW: 父親的臉還在，熱薯的味道還在。

en: Hold {key} — clear the rubble
Pulled out from under the rubble.
Your right arm is broken.
I can still carry.
That doesn't mean it isn't broken.
Sheila, Royal Wardens. One question. The blood on the bell tower — is it yours?
zh_TW: 席菈，王室巡邏隊。現在問你一件事。鐘樓上的血，是你的嗎？

en: Yes.
How many times did you ring it?
Nine.
...Eight.
The whole town heard that bell. So did I. I counted.
zh_TW: 整座鎮都聽見了那口鐘。我也聽見了。我數了。

en: Nine isn't opening a door.
It's a death knell.
Something crawls out of the crack — an Ashwalker.
zh_TW: 裂縫裡爬出了東西——灰巡者。

en: The Ninth Bell — end of the slice. Thank you for playing.
zh_TW: 第九聲鐘——切片到此結束。謝謝試玩。

en: The South Street arch. Dad used to wait for me here after school.
zh_TW: 南街的石拱。爸以前每天在這裡等我放學。

en: He'd hide behind a pillar, on purpose, so I'd have to find him.
zh_TW: 他會躲在柱子後面，故意讓我找。

en: Nothing written down yet.
